title: Egg freezing
what: The ovaries are stimulated with injections so several eggs mature. Then they are collected with a thin needle under brief anesthesia and frozen for the future.
why: When a woman wants to delay pregnancy, or before treatment that may harm the ovaries.
duration: stimulation usually takes 10 to 14 days, collection about 15 to 30 minutes; you go home the same day
tell_doctor: All medicines, especially hormones and blood thinners
If you had ovarian hyperstimulation before

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Hormone and infection tests, and an ultrasound. Your doctor will assess your egg reserve.

prepare.title: Injections
prepare.text: Hormone injections are given daily, usually by yourself at home. A nurse will teach you.

prepare.title: Monitoring
prepare.text: You come for ultrasounds and blood tests a few times. The dose is adjusted based on them.

prepare.title: Collection day
prepare.text: No food or drink for 6 hours, unless told otherwise. You need someone to take you home.

bring: Someone to take you home on collection day
steps: You give yourself injections as scheduled for 10 to 14 days
Every few days, an ultrasound shows how the follicles are growing
When they are ready, a trigger shot is given at an exact time
About 1 to 1.5 days later, collection under brief anesthesia
Guided by ultrasound, the doctor collects the eggs through the vagina with a thin needle
An embryologist checks and freezes them
You rest for 1 to 2 hours and go home
feel: The injections cause brief pain, sometimes bruises
Bloating and heaviness low in the belly during stimulation
After collection: period-like cramps and sleepiness
after: Rest on collection day. Do not drive
Cramps and spotting usually last 1 to 2 days
Your period usually comes in 1 to 2 weeks
Your doctor will tell you how many eggs were frozen
red_flags: Severe belly pain and bloating, shortness of breath, or passing little urine: call emergency services
Fast weight gain over 1 to 2 days: see a doctor urgently
Heavy bleeding or a fever over 38°C (100.4°F): see a doctor urgently

faq.q: What age is best for freezing?
faq.a: The earlier, the better the quality. Usually before 35 is advised.
No. It improves your chances in the future, but there is no guarantee.

faq.q: How long can eggs be stored?
faq.a: Many years. The clinic will tell you the storage terms.

reminders.text: Egg collection tomorrow. No food or drink for 6 hours, unless told otherwise. Give the trigger shot exactly at the set time.
